Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

abuse verb and noun

ill-treat a person or an animal

also mistreat, ill-treat, maltreat, mistreatment, ill-treatment

classical

Cato ap. Gell. 2.6.7 (Lewis & Short)
Gell. 2.6.5

vexō, vexāre, vexāvī, vexātum

verb, first conjugation

harass, ill-treat, maltreat

Properly to shake or toss about (Gellius explains it as stronger than vehere, 2.6.5); then the general word for harassing and ill-treating people, lands and things.

Other words

  • injūriōsē tractāre — treat unjustly, ill-treat

    phrase: injūriōsē with tractō, tractāre, tractāvī, tractātum · also used · classical · Cic. Imp. Pomp. 11: mercātōrēs ac nāviculāriī injūriōsius tractātī (Lewis & Short, s.v. tractō)

    Also injūriā afficere, to do someone wrong. Tractāre alone means to treat or handle, well or badly.

Examples

  • In calamitōsō rīsus etiam injūria est.

    laughing at someone in trouble is itself a wrongPublil. Syr. I 27

  • Nōlī fēlem vexāre.

    Leave the cat alone, don’t torment it.composed

See also abuse, hurt, victim.
